analysis:
Examined every supplied patch and BASE excerpt of docs/reference/protocol-messages.md. HEAD lines 171–195 introduce reversible add-on holds using draining heartbeats, optional registration/heartbeat busy metadata, unknown-reason fallback, and typed rejection of routed requests. HEAD lines 284, 383 and 1445 document the corresponding fields and autopilot busy reason. No executable implementation is supplied, so no concrete control regression is established. Existing BASE lines 118–150 distinguish lifecycle barriers and billing settlement from reversible heartbeat draining (BASE line 345); avoiding provider_drain for a hold does not itself demonstrate lost accounting or cancellation safety.
Integration should verify CoordinatorClient+Registration.swift, ProviderBusy.swift and ProtocolCodec.swift against the hold implementation: admission closes during holds, accepted work and terminal accounting remain intact, hold release cannot reopen a lifecycle-fenced or unauthorized connection, and attestation/revocation handling stays responsive (TB-002, TB-007, TB-011, T-010, T-053, T-057, A-009, A-016). The claim at HEAD lines 176–177 that registration excludes a held provider before its first heartbeat requires a matching platform contract: registration has no documented status field and the new busy fields are described as separately supported platform work. This is unverified, not evidence of a regression. Check busy_addon bounds and diagnostic sinks for untrusted strings and new activity/identifier disclosure, and review local add-on authorization under TB-003. Surrounding encryption, privacy-capability, cache-isolation and capacity-accounting documentation is unchanged; this patch supplies no evidence of changes to those controls (T-008, T-041, A-001, A-003).
